explanation: The equal prefix needs no editing. At the first mismatch there is only one possible kind of repair given the two lengths: advance both pointers for replacement, or advance only the longer string for insertion/deletion. Any later mismatch requires a second edit.
correctness: Before a mismatch, both pointers delimit equal prefixes after the edits already used. A length difference above one is impossible to repair with one edit. With equal lengths, an insertion or deletion would leave unequal lengths, so the mismatch must be replaced. With unequal lengths, only skipping the longer string's next character can align the remaining suffixes. Accepting at most one such mismatch, including a possible final extra character, is necessary and sufficient.
walkthrough: For 'plane' and 'pane', p matches p. At l versus a, the lengths differ by one, so skip only l in the longer string. The remaining a,n,e match, giving true. For 'ab' and 'ba', replacing the first mismatch leaves a second mismatch, so the result is false.
timeComplexity: O(n + m) time in the input lengths.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space, without allocating normalized or sliced copies.
edgeCases: Empty versus one character succeeds; empty versus two fails.
An extra character at either end is one edit; a transposition usually needs two.
